activity_context.topic_title: Expected Values of Discrete Random Variables

feedback.problem: A bag contains $2$ nickels ($5$¢), $4$ dimes ($10$¢), and $4$ quarters ($25$¢). If one coin is randomly drawn from a bag, what is its expected value?
feedback.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Let $X$ be the value of a randomly drawn coin. Then the support is $S={5,10,25}.$

In the bag there are $2$ nickels, $4$ dimes, and $4$ quarters (ten coins in total), so the probabilities are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(5) & =\frac{2}{10}=\frac{1}{5} \\ P(10) & =\frac{4}{10}=\frac{2}{5} \\ P(25) & =\frac{4}{10}=\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =5\cdot f(5)+10\cdot f(10)+25\cdot f(25) \\  & =5(\frac{1}{5})+10(\frac{2}{5})+25(\frac{2}{5}) \\  & =\frac{5}{5}+\frac{20}{5}+\frac{50}{5} \\  & =1+4+10 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$
